Q587584.justification: A ring of megalithic standing stones and trilithons on a simple repeated post-and-lintel module — the reason it anchors the milestone's own first (4-minute) cut.

Q215429.justification: Guild-hall facades are narrow, gabled, flat-fronted rowhouses with a repeated rectilinear module and stepped-gable silhouette — a brick abstraction of the facade line, not the ornament.

Q1175856.justification: Stepped and smooth pyramidal massing is close to the simplest solid geometry a brick medium can render.

Q131013.justification: The Parthenon's peripteral colonnade — evenly spaced columns under a plain entablature and pediment — is a textbook repeated-module classical temple.

Q9141.justification: A symmetrical domed mausoleum on a plinth with four corner minarets — a small, highly regular set of primitives (dome, cube, cylinder). Principally a tomb, not a congregational worship space; a small working mosque flanks one side but isn't the monument being abstracted.

Q3331815.justification: Dry-stone terracing and rectangular one-story structures on a hillside — coursed masonry is close to a brick module by construction, not just by analogy.

Q29070.justification: A stepped, terraced stupa mountain — concentric square-to-circular terraces stacking into one pyramidal silhouette.

Q4176.justification: Twin spires and a repeated vertical bay rhythm (buttresses, pinnacles, lancet windows) give it an unusually regular, countable Gothic module for its scale. It is a real, active cathedral with regular services — included because its exterior massing is real and simple; flagged here explicitly as the clearest active-place-of-worship case in this seed set, not silently skipped.

Q189764.justification: A three-tier Roman aqueduct of repeated round arches, diminishing in span per tier — as modular as engineering gets.

Q5788.justification: The Treasury's rock-cut facade reads, from the front, as a flat, symmetrical two-story classical colonnade with a broken pediment, even though it's carved rather than built.

Q5859.justification: El Castillo is a textbook stepped pyramid with a single square temple on top — the same primitive family as Giza/Borobudur, just stepped rather than smooth.

Q129072.justification: A raised rectangular terrace lined with rows of identical fluted columns (the Apadana) — a repeated post module.

Q237128.justification: Cliff Palace's stacked rectangular masonry rooms and towers, built into a stepped rock alcove, are a naturally blocky, coursed-stone module.

Q14863645.justification: Modernist International Style buildings (flat roofs, plain rectilinear volumes, ribbon windows) are close to the simplest possible built massing — literally boxes.

Q122026.justification: Shaft XII's steel-framed rectilinear halls and its iconic headframe tower are simple industrial box-and-tower forms.

Q189358.justification: A rectangular Renaissance fortress with four corner towers around a courtyard — simple, highly symmetrical castle massing.

Q750675.justification: A single freestanding rectangular tower (the type site is Bruges' belfry) is about the simplest possible civic monument massing — a tall box with a spire.

Q45178.justification: The shell roofs are literally derived from sections of a single sphere (Utzon's real solution to the construction problem) — a small number of repeated curved-shell primitives, unusually simple for a modern icon.

Q2844.justification: The National Congress's twin towers plus one dome and one inverted dome are close to pure geometric primitives — some of the most literally 'simple solid' civic architecture built in the 20th century.

Q1763364.justification: The moai are freestanding blocky monolithic figures on rectangular platforms (ahu) — about as simple a standing-stone module as exists, closely related to Stonehenge in spirit.

Q9427.justification: The great mudbrick mosques (Djinguereber, Sankoré) have a distinctive stepped, buttressed, blocky earthen massing with projecting toron beams. Djinguereber and Sankoré remain active mosques; included for their real, celebrated, highly legible architectural form, not for their interior as a devotional space — flagged explicitly per the active-place-of-worship review requirement.

Q29317.justification: Thousands of stepped, terraced brick stupas and temples share one architectural vocabulary — the same tiered-terrace family as Borobudur, at the scale of a whole plain.

Q188754.justification: A tiered, white-plastered castle keep with a strongly stepped, pagoda-like roofline — one of the most legible modular silhouettes in castle architecture anywhere.

Q237.justification: Bernini's colonnade around St. Peter's Square is a radial ring of repeated identical columns — a pure repeated-module structure. Scoped explicitly to the public piazza colonnade, not the Basilica's interior as an active worship space.

Q647958.justification: The Iron Bridge itself is a single, small, geometrically simple arched span — the world's first major cast-iron bridge, an obvious skeletal/brick abstraction candidate.

Q127754.justification: A real 19th/20th-century blast-furnace industrial complex — riveted steel skeletal towers and rectilinear halls, the same simple industrial-module family as Zollverein.

Q272153.justification: A rock fortress with a monolithic outcrop, a grand staircase, and rectangular terraces/gardens at its base — a blocky stepped composition on a dramatic but geometrically simple monolith.

Q209217.justification: Dry-stone curvilinear enclosure walls built from coursed granite blocks with no mortar — arguably the most direct real-world analogue to a Klemmbaustein wall in this whole list.

Q718001.justification: Circular and rectangular earthen communal roundhouses are pure ring/drum primitives — among the simplest large-scale residential building forms anywhere in the world.

Q4993586.justification: Two conical burial mounds, two runestones, and a small single-nave stone church — about as minimal a built vocabulary as any WHS gets. The church is a real, currently active parish church; included as a simple stone volume, not as a devotional space to be entered/interacted with.

Q18448486.justification: The Colosseum's tiered arcade of repeated round arches (four superimposed orders) is a highly regular, countable module — abstracting the amphitheatre drum specifically, not this designation's whole extraterritorial extent.

Q2397751.justification: Angkor Wat's central quincunx of stepped, tiered towers on a stepped platform is a repeated conical/stepped module. Angkor Wat remains an active Buddhist site with resident monks; the abstraction targets the tiered tower massing, not the interior shrine as a devotional space — flagged explicitly per the active-place-of-worship review requirement.

Q20644172.justification: Repeated narrow brick warehouse blocks along the canals, plus the Chilehaus's faceted prow — an unusually literal case of a real brick building being abstracted into a brick model.

Q15240748.justification: The real WHS-protected surface architecture (the historic timber/steel headframes and shaft-tower buildings) is a simple industrial tower form, the same family as Zollverein/Völklingen — the underground chambers themselves aren't what's being abstracted here.

Q9603543.justification: The Alcazaba's crenellated fortress walls and rectangular towers are simple defensive massing; the Nasrid palaces' famously intricate interior ornament is explicitly NOT what a brick abstraction would attempt — only the exterior fortress silhouette is in scope.

Q17117964.justification: The whole island reads, from a distance, as a single stepped-pyramid silhouette rising to the abbey spire — the same massing family as Borobudur/Giza at the scale of an entire settlement, not the intricate abbey interior.

Q15728389.justification: A double-tier Roman aqueduct of unmortared granite blocks and repeated round arches — the same simple modular family as Pont du Gard.

Q64763166.justification: A Caspian hilltop citadel (Naryn-Kala) with long parallel defensive walls running down to the sea — simple crenellated wall-and-tower massing, the same family as Kronborg.

Q172613.justification: The Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon are textbook stepped pyramids along a single axial avenue — the same primitive family as Chichen Itza/Giza, and simpler than most Maya sites' more elaborate roof-combs.

Q16913064.justification: Conical dry-stone huts (trulli) with whitewashed cylindrical walls — one of the single simplest real vernacular building forms anywhere, essentially a repeated cone-on-cylinder module.

Q192518.justification: Mudbrick tower houses rising straight-walled for several stories ("the Manhattan of the desert") — a real, famous case of extreme repeated-module verticality in earthen construction.

Q833781.justification: Vauban's star-shaped bastion fortifications are pure geometric plan-forms (angular bastions, straight ramparts) — about as literally 'simple solid geometry' as military architecture gets.

excluded.Q7341: Auschwitz-Birkenau, German Nazi Concentration and Extermination Camp: real historical site of genocide during the Holocaust — never rendered as a toy/game object.
excluded.Q231140: Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome): real site of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima and its mass civilian death toll — never rendered as a toy/game object.
excluded.Q244347: Island of Gorée: real historical site tied to the Atlantic slave trade — never rendered as a toy/game object.
excluded.Q192493: Robben Island: real site of political imprisonment and forced labour under apartheid — never rendered as a toy/game object.
excluded.Q152225: Bikini Atoll Nuclear Test Site: real site of mass displacement and nuclear weapons testing with lasting harm to its Marshallese community — never rendered as a toy/game object.
